title: Smallest Stable Index II
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the smallest index i where the difference between the maximum value in nums[0..i] and the minimum value in nums[i..n-1] is less than or equal to k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the smallest index i where the difference between the maximum value in nums[0..i] and the minimum value in nums[i..n-1] is less than or equal to k. If no such index exists, return -1.
constraints: nums is nonempty and may contain negative integers; k is any integer.
At i compare max(nums[0:i+1]) with min(nums[i:n]).
Return the smallest i whose difference is at most k, or -1.
hints: Precompute the minimum of every suffix.
Scan left to right while maintaining the maximum of the current prefix.
The first index satisfying prefix_max-suffix_min≤k is the required answer.
Both summaries exactly cover the ranges in the definition, and scan order guarantees the smallest qualifying index.
editorial: Both summaries exactly cover the ranges in the definition, and scan order guarantees the smallest qualifying index.

tests.explanation: Only index three has prefix maximum five and suffix minimum four within difference three; return three.
At index zero, prefix maximum and suffix minimum are both -5, so return zero.
